facts.journal: Journal of Esthetic and Restorative Dentistry
facts.population: 37 patients (130 teeth) restored with extensive anterior ceramic veneers in a private practice
facts.intervention: Extensive adhesively luted heat-pressed ceramic veneers (Cergo) with etch-and-rinse adhesive and dual-curing composite cement
outcomes: effect of veneer position and dentin exposure
facts.main_result: 36-month Kaplan-Meier survival was 95.1% and success 92.8%; veneers with >50% exposed dentin had a higher intervention risk (HR 10.6, p = 0.026) but no survival effect, and jaw position had no influence.
facts.funding_coi: Authors report no financial interest in the companies whose materials were used
facts.key_finding: After 36 months, extensive heat-pressed ceramic veneers in a private practice had a 95.1% survival rate and 92.8% success rate, with ceramic fracture the main failure cause. Upper and lower jaw performed alike, while veneers with more than 50% exposed dentin needed significantly more interventions.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Extensive pressable ceramic veneers can be placed on mandibular as well as maxillary anterior teeth, but large exposed dentin areas raise the risk of recementation or endodontic intervention.

facts.population: 31 patients (101 teeth) with extended anterior veneers placed in a private practice
facts.intervention: Extended adhesively luted heat-pressed glass-ceramic veneers (Cergo)
facts.comparison: Veneers with >50% vs <50% exposed dentin; maxilla vs mandible
outcomes: effect of jaw position and dentin exposure
facts.main_result: 7-year Kaplan-Meier survival was 93.6% and success 84.3%; >50% exposed dentin increased intervention risk (HR 3.71, P = .0041) without affecting survival; jaw position had no influence.
materials_brands: Variolink (Ivoclar Vivadent) and Calibra (Dentsply Sirona) dual-curing cements
facts.key_finding: After a mean of 7 years, extended heat-pressed glass-ceramic veneers had a 93.6% survival rate and 84.3% success rate, with ceramic fracture the main failure cause. Jaw position did not matter, but veneers on more than 50% exposed dentin needed significantly more clinical interventions.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Extended pressable veneers perform comparably in upper and lower anterior teeth, but dentin exposure above 50% of the preparation should be avoided or managed because it raises intervention risk.

facts.population: 31 patients (101 teeth) with extended anterior ceramic laminate veneers placed in a private practice
facts.intervention: Adhesively luted heat-pressed leucite-reinforced glass-ceramic extended anterior laminate veneers (Cergo)
facts.comparison: Veneers with >50% vs ≤50% exposed dentin; maxilla vs mandible
outcomes: effect of jaw position and dentin exposure
facts.main_result: 10-year survival was 91.8% and success 78.6%; >50% exposed dentin raised intervention risk (HR 2.98, P = .019; success 68.0%) without affecting survival; jaw position had no influence.
materials_brands: Variolink (Ivoclar Vivadent) and Calibra (Dentsply Sirona) dual-curing luting agents
facts.funding_coi: Authors report no financial interest in the companies whose materials were used
facts.limitations: Retrospective design with broad indications, varied preparation designs, loss of patients to follow-up, single operator
facts.key_finding: After a mean of about 10 years, extended heat-pressed laminate veneers had a 91.8% survival rate and 78.6% success rate, with ceramic fracture the main failure cause and debonding the main complication. Mandibular and maxillary veneers performed alike, but veneers on more than 50% exposed dentin had a significantly higher intervention risk.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: Extended veneers are a reasonable alternative to anterior full crowns, even in the mandible, but dentin exposure should be avoided or managed with different conditioning or luting strategies.
